bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM inaugurates first phase of Karbigahiya-Mithapur flyover, Mithapur-Sipara elevated ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar CM inaugurates first phase of Karbigahiya-Mithapur flyover, Mithapur-Sipara elevated road in Patna ANI | Updated: Aug 28, 2026 20:14 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna ( Bihar ) [India], August 28 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Friday inaugurated the first phase of the Karbigahiya-Mithapur flyover and the 2.1-km Mithapur-Sipara elevated road, aimed at easing traffic congestion and improving connectivity to Patna railway station, Mithapur bus stand and surrounding areas, the Bihar Chief Minister's Office (CMO) said. According to the Bihar CMO, the Karbigahiya-Mithapur flyover, including its approach and service roads connecting Mithapur Bus Stand to Mithapur Roundabout via the newly constructed Karbigahiya Roundabout, has been built at a cost of Rs 249 crore. The Chief Minister inaugurated the project by cutting the ribbon and unveiling the plaque. He also inaugurated the 2.1-km elevated road section from Mithapur to Sipara under the Mithapur-Mahuli-Punpun project. The two projects will improve traffic movement on the vital route and provide relief from congestion on Mithapur-Sipara, Karbigahiya, Mithapur and Station Road, as per CMO. The newly constructed Karbigahiya Roundabout is expected to reduce traffic pressure in the area and make commuting easier for railway passengers and the general public. After the inauguration, Choudhary inspected the newly built flyover and traffic arrangements both on foot and by vehicle. He also reviewed the facilities and traffic flow systems associated with the projects. The Chief Minister said the opening of the Karbigahiya-Mithapur flyover would make commuting to and from the railway station much easier for passengers. "People travelling to and from the Mithapur bus stand and surrounding areas will benefit from improved connectivity. Commuting towards Punpun from Mithapur via Mahuli will also become easier," he said. The elevated corridor will facilitate smoother traffic movement and help reduce vehicular congestion on major routes, he added. The two projects are significant steps towards improving the traffic system in the state capital and ensuring smooth, safe and seamless commuting for citizens, as per CMO. Deputy Chief Minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav, Road Construction Minister Kumar Shailendra, Cooperation Minister Ramkripal Yadav, MLA Shyam Rajak, MLA Arun Manjhi, MLC Naval Kishore Yadav, MLC Ravindra Prasad Singh and other public representatives were present on the occasion. Chief Minister's Principal Secretary Deepak Kumar, Road Construction Department Secretary Pankaj Kumar Pal, Inspector General of Police ( Patna Zone) Jitendra Rana, Patna District Magistrate Kundan Kumar, Senior Superintendent of Police Kartikeya K. Sharma, Chairman of Bihar State Bridge Construction Corporation Ltd Dharmendra Kumar, Managing Director of Bihar State Road Development Corporation Ltd Saurabh Jorwal and other senior officials and dignitaries were also present. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar to Open JEEViKA-Sudha Sales Centres Across All Panchayats - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar to Open JEEViKA-Sudha Sales Centres Across All Panchayats 28 Aug 2026 2 min read Why in News? Bihar is set to establish JEEViKA-Sudha sales centres across all 8,053 panchayats under Saat Nischay-3 to provide better market access to JEEViKA Didis , strengthen milk-based rural businesses and create new opportunities for women-led livelihoods. Key Points JEEViKA-Sudha Sales Centres: Sales centres will be established across all 8,053 panchayats of Bihar. The initiative is being implemented under Saat Nischay-3 . Sudha Sakhis will be selected through milk producers’ cooperative societies across all 8,053 panchayats. Support: Selected JEEViKA Didis will receive equipment such as a 300-litre deep freezer, Visi Cooler, sunboard, apron and cap. Training: Selected Sudha Sakhis are proposed to receive training under the Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme . COMFED is accelerating the formation of primary milk producers’ cooperative societies under Saat Nischay-3. Direct Payment: DPMCU systems are being installed to facilitate direct payment of milk prices into producers’ bank accounts. Bihar plans to establish 534 animal medicine sales centres , with one centre in every block. The Centre has given initial approval for 109 animal medicine centres . Mithila Handicrafts: The state has established the Mithila Handicrafts Cooperative Society to support women artisans through markets, branding, training and financial opportunities. Global Market: Bihar plans to explore the export and marketing of Mithila handicrafts in the Angkor Wat region of Cambodia. bihar_raw_news.title: Parliamentary Panel To Review Bihar Air Connectivity And Heritage - RAHSTA Expo 2026
bihar_raw_news.content: Parliamentary Panel To Review Bihar Air Connectivity And Heritage Infrastructure Transport Aug 28 2026 The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture, chaired by Janata Dal (United) leader Sanjay Jha, began a three-day visit to Bihar to prioritise enhancement of air and road connectivity, preservation of cultural heritage and development of tourism infrastructure. The delegation planned detailed discussions on expansion of airports and air connectivity, including the international greenfield airport announced in the Union Budget, as well as national highway and road projects across the state. Specific road corridors to be reviewed include the Patna–Purnia route and the Gorakhpur–Siliguri link, and attention would be paid to stretches of NH-27 reported to be in poor condition. The panel also intended to scrutinise maintenance arrangements for museums, the Khuda Bakhsh Library and historical sites managed by the Archaeological Survey of India such as Kumrahar, and on-site inspections were scheduled at the Bihar Museum in Patna and key heritage and pilgrimage centres in and around Gaya, Rajgir and Nalanda. The committee was scheduled to travel to Gaya on Monday evening and to hold a tourism-focused meeting the following day to discuss development at destinations including Bodh Gaya and Rajgir alongside projects announced in the Union Budget. Members underlined the potential of tourism to generate employment and to act as a catalyst for wider economic development in Bihar, and the panel stated that it would compile observations and recommendations for submission to Parliament. Following submission of its report the relevant central departments were expected to proceed with follow up action and timelines for project implementation would be decided after detailed discussions with state and central officers. The visit was described as an opportunity to review centrally funded schemes and to seek clearer milestones for advancement of transport connectivity, tourism and cultural conservation in the state. Around them sit girls who had never held a mouse, women who had never opened an email, and government school students who knew the internet only as a neighbour’s phone. The room is called YUG LAB. It was built by a schoolgirl in England. Esanika Chauhan, a Year 12 student at Charterhouse School in the United Kingdom, launched YUG LAB in January 2025 in association with KCS Foundation India. Eighteen months later, the project has reached more than 2,200 students, women and girls across Samastipur, Darbhanga and Sitamarhi — districts where digital exclusion has long been the quiet tax on ambition. Not charity. Curriculum. What separates YUG LAB from the familiar story of donated computers is that Esanika did not stop at the hardware. She wrote the course herself, building it around what a rural learner actually needs on a Monday morning rather than what a syllabus says they should know: • Creating flyers and posters — turning a self-help group, a tuition class or a small shop into something that can advertise itself • Navigating Government of India and state government digital schemes — so entitlements stop being rumours in a queue and become applications with a reference number • Safe social media — privacy settings, fraud and impersonation, and the confidence to be online without being prey • Everyday office skills — typing, files and folders, email, and producing a document that looks professional Teaching the economy, not just the interface The newest strand of the curriculum is the one Esanika is most insistent about: a computer is only useful if it earns something. Advertisement Learners are taught to keep a household or shop ledger in a spreadsheet, to price a product by working backwards from cost, and to understand what interest does to a borrowed rupee over a year. Digital payments are taught alongside the arithmetic behind them — what a transaction record proves, why a savings habit compounds, and how a self-help group’s books should look when a bank officer asks to see them. For women who have run small enterprises for years on memory alone, the shift is the difference between a business that can be described and one that can be financed. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM conducts aerial survey of flood-hit Nepal border areas - The Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: August 28, 2026 Bihar CM conducts aerial survey of flood-hit Nepal border areas Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Thursday conducted an aerial survey of the flood-affected areas in the state that shares a border with Nepal, where devastating flash floods claimed the lives of at least 162 people and left many untraceable a day ago. After the aerial inspection at Valmikinagar in West Champaran district, he said Prime Minister Narendra Modi was monitoring the situation. Bihar was put on alert as floodwaters from the neighbouring country entered the Gandak River and reached the Gandak barrage on Wednesday, prompting authorities to open all 36 gates to control the surge. In a post on social media, Choudhary wrote, “In view of the floods in Nepal, I conducted an aerial survey of the flood situation in Bihar’s border areas, including Bagaha, Valmikinagar, Bettiah, and Motihari. I also reviewed the administrative preparedness regarding the potential impact, necessary precautionary measures, safety, and relief and rescue operations.” He also directed the officials concerned to take all necessary steps with utmost promptness and preparedness. Ensuring the safety of citizens in flood-affected areas and providing them with every possible assistance remains the highest priority of the state Government, Choudhary said. Talking to reporters, the CM said, “With the blessings of the Almighty, things are returning to normalcy. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is monitoring the situation. The discharge of water from the Gandak barrage has started declining. Due to fresh rainfall, the water level in the Gandak River has increased slightly, but the discharge from the barrage is still around 1 lakh cusecs.” The water discharge from the Gandak barrage at Valmikinagar declined from 1.50 lakh cusecs at 11 pm on Wednesday to 1.04 lakh cusecs on Thursday morning. “The water discharge from the Gandak barrage at Valmikinagar peaked at 1.50 lakh cusecs at 11 pm on Wednesday, after which the water level began receding,” said the Water Resources Department (WRD) in a statement on Thursday. The water level of the Gandak River, which was in spate after the flash floods in Nepal a day ago, was showing a receding trend on Thursday, bringing respite to the residents of low-lying areas in northern parts of Bihar, officials said. The Nepal Police said that the death toll rose to 162 in the flash floods on the Bhotekoshi river that wreaked havoc across three districts of the neighbouring country on Wednesday. The flash floods were caused after an avalanche blocked the flow of the Lhende tributary of the Bhotekoshi river and first hit Timure, near Nepal’s border with China, at Rasuwagadhi. 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar sugarcane mechanisation scheme draws over 4600 farmers, 110 farmer groups
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News Patna: Bihar’s Sugarcane Mechanisation Scheme 2026-27 has so far attracted more than 4,600 farmers and 110 farmer groups, with the initiative aimed at reducing cultivation costs and improving productivity through modern agricultural technology, reported Indian Masterminds. Eligible farmers with a valid Sugarcane Farmer ID can submit applications through the Cane Care Portal or SUMEK Portal to receive subsidies from the Bihar Sugarcane Industries Department on 44 types of agricultural machinery used for land preparation, sowing, irrigation, weed control, harvesting and crop-residue management. Farmers can receive assistance for up to three agricultural machines. They can also receive a subsidy of up to 40% on eligible machinery, while those belonging to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Extremely Backward Classes are eligible for an additional 10% subsidy, taking the maximum assistance to 50%. Support is also available for value-addition equipment, including sugarcane juice machines. For crop-residue management equipment and set-treatment devices, assistance can reach 75% for general-category farmers and 80% for SC, ST and EBC farmers. Eligible groups and institutions setting up machinery banks to help small and marginal farmers access modern equipment can apply through SUMEK Portal to receive assistance of up to 80% of project costs, capped at Rs 8 lakh for projects costing up to Rs 10 lakh. PACS, JEEViKA groups, ATMA-registered farmer groups, FPOs, agri-tech companies and societies, Agricultural Technical Service Providers, licensed jaggery entrepreneurs, sugar mills and relevant government institutions are eligible to apply. The department has urged eligible farmers to apply soon. The initiative is aimed at reducing dependence on manual labour, improving farm efficiency and crop quality, and strengthening farmers’ incomes through greater mechanisation.

bihar_raw_news.title: Europe tightens rules for investment-based citizenship programmes | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: August 27, 2026 Europe tightens rules for investment-based citizenship programmes Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Agency For years, several European countries used investment migration programmes to attract foreign capital. Applicants could obtain citizenship or residency by investing in property, businesses, government funds or national development projects. That approach is changing. European institutions and national governments are placing greater emphasis on security, transparency and the idea that citizenship should reflect a genuine connection to a country. In April 2025, the Court of Justice of the European Union ruled that Malta’s investor citizenship scheme violated EU law because citizenship could not be granted as the direct result of a commercial transaction. The judgment significantly strengthened Europe’s position against so-called golden passport programmes. Citizenship by Investment Versus Golden Visas Citizenship by investment and residence by investment are often discussed as if they were the same, but they provide different rights. A citizenship-by-investment programme grants nationality, usually after an applicant makes a qualifying financial contribution and passes the required checks. When citizenship is granted by an EU member state, the person also gains EU citizenship and its associated rights. A golden visa, by comparison, normally provides a residence permit rather than immediate citizenship. It may allow an investor and eligible family members to live in a country, but citizenship generally requires several years of residence, language ability and evidence of integration. This distinction matters because Europe’s strongest legal objections have focused on direct citizenship schemes. Golden visas remain available in some countries, although they are also facing tighter controls. Why European Authorities Are Tightening the Rules European policymakers have raised concerns that poorly managed investment migration programmes can create opportunities for money laundering, tax evasion, corruption and security failures. The rights attached to EU citizenship also extend beyond the country issuing the passport. A decision made by one member state can give an individual access to movement and settlement rights across much of the European Union. Authorities therefore argue that weak screening in one country can create consequences for every member state. Russia’s invasion of Ukraine added urgency to the debate. It increased scrutiny of whether sanctioned individuals or politically exposed persons could use investment routes to gain access to Europe. The European Commission has since continued monitoring investor residence schemes and their safeguards. New Compliance and Due-Diligence Requirements Investors should now expect more detailed checks covering their identity, financial history and source of wealth. Authorities may request bank records, company documents, tax returns and evidence explaining how investment funds were earned. Applications can also be examined for political exposure, sanctions, criminal allegations and reputational concerns. Family members and business associates may receive additional scrutiny where necessary. For applicants, the process is becoming less about simply meeting an investment threshold and more about proving legitimacy at every stage. Specialist advisory firms such as Savory&Partners may help applicants understand programme requirements and organise documentation, but the final decision always rests with the relevant government. Professional guidance cannot replace accurate disclosure or official due diligence.

bihar_raw_news.title: Sidharth Malhotra's The Vvaan Inspired By Bihar's Vandevi Temple - MensXP
bihar_raw_news.content: Bollywood Updated on Aug 28, 2026, 09:44 IST 0 All About Mysterious Vandevi Temple In Bihar That Inspired Sidharth Malhotra's The Vvaan By Aman Kumar Sidharth Malhotra’s The Vvaan: Force Of The Forrest has unveiled a world steeped in Indian folklore, mystery and supernatural forces. The teaser opens with a forbidden forest and a chilling warning against entering it after sunset. Sidharth is seen drawn towards the mysterious woods, while Tamannaah Bhatia appears as his wife. The glimpse features strange occurrences, a divine presence and ominous forces, culminating in the promise of a battle against evil. © TVF But did you know that the makers have rooted the film in the folklore of Bihar’s Vandevi Temple in Bihta, giving the story a distinctly local flavour. About The Vandevi Folklore That Inspired The Vvaan Temple Is Closed After The Sunset About The Vandevi Folklore That Inspired The Vvaan Located around 30–35 kilometres from Patna, the Maa Vandevi Temple stands near the triangular boundary of Amhara, Raghopur and Kanchanpur villages in Bihta. The shrine is believed to be around 350-400 years old and is unusual because the deity is worshipped not through a conventional idol, but in the form of a sacred pind . According to local folklore, the shrine's origins are connected to Maa Vindhyavasini of Vindhyachal. Devotee and spiritual figure Vidyanand Mishra, who worshipped Vindhyavasini, reportedly found it difficult to travel to Vindhyachal in his old age. Legend says the goddess appeared to him in a dream and instructed him to bring a portion of her sacred pind to his village. Mishra subsequently brought the pind to the forested area near Raghopur and Kanchanpur, where he established it and began worshipping it. Since the shrine was surrounded by dense forest, the goddess came to be known as Van Devi, or the Goddess of the Forest. © Instagram/uniquepatna The temple's physical structure evolved much later. Initially, the sacred pind was housed beneath a simple hut. In 1958, saint Bhagwan Das Tyagi, who had come to Amhara for a yajna, helped transform the site into a temple. From February 12, 1997, local devotees undertook further construction, eventually creating the larger shrine seen today. Temple Is Closed After The Sunset One of its most intriguing beliefs concerns sunset. Traditionally, after the temple doors were closed, the priest would leave and nobody remained nearby. Local devotees believe that Maa Vandevi herself then roams the temple premises. Whether viewed as faith or folklore, this mysterious tradition forms part of the shrine's enduring cultural identity and provides a fascinating real-world foundation for The Vvaan . Meanwhile, The Vvaan , directed by Deepak Mishra and starring Sidharth, Tamannaah and Sunil Grover, is slated for release on September 25. bihar_raw_news.title: Nations need resilient supply chains and rapid innovation to fight protracted conflicts: Rajnath
bihar_raw_news.content: August 28, 2026 Nations need resilient supply chains and rapid innovation to fight protracted conflicts: Rajnath Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Nations with resilient supply chains, strong industrial capacity and ability to innovate rapidly would be better equipped to withstand prolonged conflicts, said Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Thursday in the backdrop of the more than four-year-old Russia-Ukraine war. Against this backdrop, he said the Centre was committed to ensuring that India’s armed forces were not dependent on foreign supply chains for critical defence requirements. “Our aim is to manufacture defence equipment domestically, undertake repair and maintenance within the country, upgrade existing systems with modern technologies, and develop next-generation capabilities indigenously,” Singh maintained. He said these efforts reflected India’s emergence as a global manufacturing hub, a reliable technology partner and a trusted defence partner. Singh made the remarks after laying the foundation stone of a `472-crore facility for the overhaul of T-series battle tanks at the 57-year-old Vehicle Factory Jabalpur (VFJ). Highlighting the changing nature of warfare, he noted countries possessing advanced technologies, resilient supply chains, robust industrial capabilities and dynamic innovation ecosystems would be in a stronger position to sustain themselves during long-drawn conflicts. Singh said the T-series tank overhaul facility would help build a resilient domestic supply chain by generating demand for a wide range of mechanical, electrical, electronic and hydraulic components, assemblies and subsystems. “The sourcing of these items would create opportunities for local MSMEs in manufacturing and ancillary services associated with tank overhauling, while helping develop a strong and self-sustaining industrial ecosystem,” he stated. The project would prove to be a boon for soldiers and generate employment opportunities in Jabalpur and surrounding areas, including for workers, youth, small entrepreneurs and other sections of the local population, Singh said. He emphasised that while warfare was rapidly changing with the advent of drones, precision-guided weapons, missiles, satellites, artificial intelligence and cyber warfare, the relevance of tanks had not diminished, but only evolved. “Modern warfare demands combined capabilities rather than dependence on a single platform. Tanks, infantry, artillery, drones, air power, surveillance and precision weapons together form an integrated combat system,” he pointed out. Singh emphasised there was a need to equip tanks with superior sensors and capabilities suited to the requirements of the modern battlefield. “Our focus is to provide soldiers with drones, missiles, artillery, electronic warfare capabilities, energy weapons and modernised tanks, while ensuring seamless coordination among them. This overhaul facility will advance this vision,” he said. bihar_raw_news.title: Nepal floods bring back Bihar's biggest fear: Why the Kosi River, known as 'sorrow of Bihar ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Nepal floods bring back Bihar’s biggest fear: Why the Kosi River, known as ‘sorrow of Bihar’, remains uncontrollable From devastating floods to sudden changes in its path, the Kosi River has remained one of Bihar’s biggest monsoon challenges. Here’s why this Himalayan river is so difficult to control. Pratik Parthsarthi August 28, 2026 / 10:19 IST Nepal floods Kosi River is Bihar's "Sorrow" due to flood risk. High sediment load causes riverbed to rise. River avulsion (course change) makes floods unpredictable. Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan Register for FREE Webinar Register for FREE A catastrophic flash flood and debris flow hit the Nepal-Tibet border region on August 26, killing more than 450 people and leaving over 1,000 others missing. The disaster has raised concerns in neighbouring Indian states, especially Bihar, which shares river systems and a long border with Nepal. While the immediate threat from rivers like the Gandak has reduced after water levels started declining, the larger Himalayan river network continues to pose a recurring flood risk for Bihar during the monsoon season. Among these rivers, the Kosi stands out as one of the most feared. Popularly known as the “Sorrow of Bihar”, the river is not dangerous only because of overflowing waters. Over the years, the Kosi has triggered some of Bihar’s worst flood disasters, including the major floods of 1954, 1968 and 2008. The 2008 flood, in particular, saw the river breach its embankment in Nepal and shift to an old channel, affecting millions of people across Bihar. But what makes the Kosi so unstable, and why does it continue to remain a major challenge for flood management in Bihar? The Kosi River: Himalayan giant with a dangerous nature The Kosi, known as Saptakoshi in Nepal, is formed by the meeting of several rivers originating from the Himalayas and Tibetan plateau. Its major tributaries include the Sun Koshi, Arun Koshi and Tamur Koshi, which merge at Triveni in Nepal before the river enters Bihar and eventually joins the Ganga. The river basin stretches across a dramatic landscape, from Himalayan regions rising nearly 8,000 metres above sea level to the flat plains of Bihar at around 60 metres. This sharp change in elevation plays a major role in the river’s behaviour. While flowing through the mountains, the Kosi carries huge amounts of sand, rocks and sediment due to erosion, landslides and intense rainfall. When it reaches the plains, the river slows down and starts depositing much of this material. According to a 2019 study by the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), the Kosi is an “extremely dynamic” river system with frequent flooding. The study estimated that the river carries nearly 100 million tonnes of sediment annually at Chatara in Nepal. Why does the Kosi carry massive amounts of silt? The answer lies in the young and unstable Himalayan landscape. The Himalayas are still rising, making them highly vulnerable to erosion.

bihar_raw_news.title: Kolkata Water Flows Face Fresh Farakka Pressure - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Cities Kolkata Kolkata Water Flows Face Fresh Farakka Pressure Kolkata Urban news Water Management Kolkata Water Flows Face Fresh Farakka Pressure By UrbanPost August 28, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Kolkata Water Flows Face Fresh Farakka Pressure Kolkata’s water and river systems are again drawing attention as rising Ganga levels in Bihar trigger changes in the operation of the Farakka Barrage in West Bengal. The development matters beyond the flood situation upstream: Farakka regulates part of the Ganga flow feeding the Bhagirathi-Hooghly system, which has long been linked to Kolkata’s port, navigation and freshwater conditions. The Bihar government recently asked West Bengal to open all gates of the barrage as Ganga levels rose above danger marks in several locations. West Bengal subsequently opened the gates, according to official reports. The immediate objective was to increase downstream river movement and reduce pressure in flood-affected areas of Bihar.For Kolkata, the significance lies in how closely the city remains connected to a river system managed hundreds of kilometres upstream. Farakka is around 300 km north of Kolkata and was built to divert Ganga water into the Bhagirathi-Hooghly system. Its feeder canal can carry about 40,000 cusecs, supporting the river system on which Kolkata’s historic port and navigation network depend.That makes barrage operations an infrastructure issue as much as a flood-management decision. Changes in river flows can affect navigation, sediment movement and the wider ecological balance of the Hooghly. The Farakka project itself identifies improving the Bhagirathi-Hooghly system, reducing salinity and supporting water availability around Kolkata among its core functions. The latest episode also highlights a wider weakness in managing river-dependent cities. Kolkata’s flood risks are not determined by upstream barrage operations alone. Local rainfall, drainage capacity, tidal conditions, siltation and the condition of outfall channels all influence urban flooding. West Bengal’s own flood-management assessment notes that the Bhagirathi-Hooghly basin faces drainage constraints and that tidal conditions can worsen flood impacts.That distinction is important for the city. A higher river flow does not automatically translate into better flood protection for Kolkata, just as opening a barrage cannot by itself resolve Bihar’s flood pressures. Decisions need to account for the entire river basin, including communities living along vulnerable banks and the downstream urban economy. Kolkata is already investing in more localised flood resilience, including restoration of water bodies, improved pumping infrastructure, drainage upgrades and flood-warning systems. The Farakka episode reinforces why those measures need to sit alongside coordinated basin-level water management.For Kolkata, the immediate issue is not simply how much water moves through the Hooghly, but whether river, drainage and flood decisions across the basin are coordinated closely enough to protect people, livelihoods and critical urban infrastructure. national_raw_news.content: The death toll in devastating Nepal-Tibet flash floods has risen to 392, while 1,468 people remain missing on both sides of the border. Of the 392 people killed in the disaster, 389 died in Nepal and three in neighbouring Tibet. Nepal authorities reported 910 people missing, while officials in Tibet said another 558 people remained unaccounted for, taking the total number of missing people on the two sides of the border to 1,468. As rescuers search riverbanks and isolated settlements for survivors and recover bodies carried downstream, the threat is far from over. A newly formed barrier lake near the source of the Bhote Koshi river system has raised fears that a breach could unleash another surge, potentially worsening the disaster and complicating rescue operations already underway. Nepalese security personnel have evacuated more than 800 people from affected districts. The catastrophe has triggered a major rescue effort by India, with the External Affairs Ministry saying 290 Indian nationals in Nepal remain uncontactable. New Delhi is making “urgent efforts” to ascertain their whereabouts and coordinate their rescue, with the missing Indians including hydropower workers and tourist groups from different states. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said urgent efforts are underway to ascertain the status and well-being of Indians caught in the flood-hit areas. He said the External Affairs Ministry is coordinating with the Nepalese side, other ministries, state governments, tour operators and relevant authorities. The External Affairs Ministry has also established a 24-hour control room to assist with tracing and evacuation efforts. India has so far rescued 84 nationals. This includes 63 workers from the Trishuli-I run-of-river hydroelectric project and 21 people from Tamil Nadu.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | Business 67 World’s largest financial inclusion initiative – Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana completes 1...
national_raw_news.content: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana has completed 12 years today, marking a significant milestone in transforming the country’s financial inclusion landscape. The scheme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on this day in 2014. Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, more than 59 crore accounts have been opened so far, with total deposits amounting to 3 lakh 17 thousand crore rupees. As the world’s largest financial inclusion initiative, the scheme continues to redefine access to banking for all Indians. The average deposit per account is 5,356 rupees. Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, 78 per cent of the accounts have been opened in rural or semi-urban areas, and approximately 56 per cent of accounts are owned by women. Over 41 crore RuPay cards have been issued to Jan Dhan account holders. The scheme has also empowered millions, particularly the marginalised sections, to access banking and financial services to improve their socio-economic conditions. The Jan-Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile (JAM) trinity, with Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana at its core, has proven to be a diversion-proof mechanism for the direct delivery of financial assistance. Due to initiatives like Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, India’s Financial Inclusion Index has risen from 53.9 in 2018 to 67 in 2026, showcasing deeper access to credit, insurance, savings and digital payments. As the world’s largest financial inclusion initiative, the scheme is redefining access to banking for millions of underprivileged citizens.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | National 101 Festival of Raksha Bandhan being celebrated across the country
national_raw_news.content: Raksha Bandhan, the festival of the special bond between brothers and sisters, is being celebrated today across the country. On this occasion, sisters tie colourful Rakhi around the wrist of their brothers and pray for their prosperity, health and well-being. In return, brothers pledge to protect and support their sisters and present them gifts. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has greeted the people on the occasion of Raksha Bandhan today. In a social media post, Mr Modi expressed hope that the festival of Raksha Bandhan brings happiness, prosperity and success to everyone’s lives. He also wished that the bond of love, affection and mutual trust remains strong and unbreakable forever. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has extended greetings to countrymen on the occasion of Raksha Bandhan. In his message, Mr Birla said the festival celebrates the mutual love, affection, and trust between brothers and sisters. He noted that the festival symbolises India’s rich culture, family values, and the unbreakable bonds of affection and belonging. The Lok Sabha Speaker added that Raksha Bandhan is not merely a festival of tying a sacred thread of protection but is a celebration of trust, respect, love, and the lifelong commitment to stand by one another. He said that the bond between a brother and sister is considered one of the purest relationships in the world, as there is neither selfishness nor any condition attached to this relationship. He underlined that in India’s culture, the meaning of protection is not limited merely to ensuring the safety of sisters but also represents a commitment to protecting the respect, dignity, rights, and dreams of women. The Lok Sabha Speaker emphasised that when every daughter and every sister in society is safe, respected, and able to move forward with confidence, the nation will become truly stronger and more empowered. He urged everyone to take the resolve to always preserve love, trust, and open communication within families.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | International 74 Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman to be on 6-day visit to US beginning today
national_raw_news.content: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman will be on a six-day visit to the United States beginning today. During her visit to the US, she will travel to Chicago, Asheville and New York. In Chicago, Finance Minister will participate in a Roundtable Conference with prominent investors and engage with leading CEOs, Presidents and senior representatives of the private sector. Bilateral one-to-one meetings with CEOs and senior leadership of select companies in Chicago will also be held. The discussions will focus on India’s investment opportunities, economic outlook and areas for strengthening business and investment partnerships between India and the United States. Ms Sitharaman will also visit the Polsky Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation at the University of Chicago, where she will exchange perspectives on entrepreneurship, innovation, technology commercialisation and strengthening linkages with India’s rapidly expanding startup and innovation ecosystem. The Finance Minister will also interact with members of the Indian community in Chicago during her visit. In Asheville, Ms Sitharaman will lead the Indian delegation at the G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors Meeting under the United States Presidency of the G20. The meeting, scheduled for 31st August and 1st September, will bring together Finance Ministers, Central Bank Governors and senior economic officials from G20 members to deliberate on key global economic and financial issues. The meeting follows the G20 Finance and Central Bank Deputies Meeting scheduled for 29th and 30th August. The engagement will also provide an opportunity for India to advance its perspectives on contemporary global economic challenges and strengthen cooperation with G20 partners. In New York, Ms Sitharaman will participate in an Investor Roundtable with CEOs and senior representatives of leading New York-based companies. She will also hold one-to-one meetings with senior executives and CEOs from the financial sector to discuss investment opportunities, India’s economic and financial landscape, and avenues for strengthening financial and institutional linkages between India and the United States. During her visit to New York, NASDAQ, a pioneering global electronic marketplace and one of the world’s leading technology-driven financial market platforms, will host Ms Sitharaman in the bell-ringing ceremony. The visit will conclude on the 2nd of the next month. The finance minister is on a 9-day visit to Canada and the US, which began on August 25. In the first leg of her visit, Ms Sitharaman focused on strengthening India-Canada economic ties. In Canada, she attended the inaugural India-Canada Economic and Financial Dialogue in Toronto and also met investors and businesses from sectors including energy, artificial intelligence and critical minerals. The discussions focused on strengthening economic and financial cooperation and creating greater opportunities for investment and business between the two countries.
